I'll look through the notes folder first so the rename scheme and index match what's already there.The minutes are all 2026 committee meetings, but the filenames mix dates, words, and one postponed meeting. I’ll plan a single date-based rename and a short index, and leave the minute text as it is.Rename every file in `notes/` to the date the meeting was held, and add `notes/README.md` as a chronological index. Leave the minute text unchanged. Leave the root `README.md` and `members.csv` alone.

## Naming

Use `YYYY-MM-DD.md`. The year is 2026 in every heading. Take the date from the heading, which is the day the meeting happened.

| Current file | New file | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aug11.md` | `2026-08-11.md` | 11 August |
| `minutes 25 aug.md` | `2026-08-26.md` | Held 26 August; the file name is the cancelled Monday |
| `Meeting sept 8.md` | `2026-09-08.md` | 8 September |
| `notes_2026-09-22.md` | `2026-09-22.md` | Drop the `notes_` prefix |
| `oct6 meeting notes.md` | `2026-10-06.md` | 6 October |
| `2026.10.20 minutes.md` | `2026-10-20.md` | Same date, ISO form |
| `Nov 3 (final).md` | `2026-11-03.md` | 3 November; "final" stays out of the name |

Nothing else in the repo links to these names. This folder is not a git repo, so the renames are plain moves.

## Index

Add `notes/README.md`: a short heading, one line that files are named by the day the meeting was held, then the seven meetings oldest first. Each line links the file and gives a one-line subject drawn from that minute (noticeboard, roof, fees, gate, compost, work day, and so on). The 26 August line notes that the meeting moved from 25 August because of the storm. The 3 November line notes that it was the last meeting of the year.
